locator.title: Стоит ли покупать квартиру сейчас: мнение экспертов
locator.lead: Почему россияне активно покупают недвижимость в Москве и откуда берут средства
locator.caption: Если не планируете переезд в ближайшее время, можно купить квартиру в строящемся доме: это выгоднее, чем готовая недвижимость

current_heading.text: Почему 2026 год может быть удачным для покупки

nearest_text_before.text: Листайте галерею, чтобы посмотреть на строящиеся проекты Level 👇🏻

nearest_text_after.text: Таким образом, россияне в 2026 году не боятся покупать квартиры и улучшать свои жилищные условия. При этом многие отдают предпочтение комфортным лотам с большой площадью и интересными планировками, например с мастер-спальней или отдельной игровой для детей. К тому же покупатели рассматривают приобретение недвижимости и как выгодный актив, который может приумножить доход в будущем.

image_reading: A high-rise residential building is visibly under construction, framed frontally with exposed concrete floors and two tower cranes.
The cranes, unfinished upper levels, and active construction site make ongoing progress the natural motion; nearby completed apartment blocks provide urban context.
analysis.article_context: Gallery image 1 illustrates the article’s point that buying an apartment while a residential building is still under construction can be more advantageous than purchasing completed housing.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: The animation supports the practical appeal of purchasing a future apartment in a residential project that is visibly progressing toward completion.
structured_intent.primary_action: Construction equipment steadily advances work upward on the unfinished residential tower.
structured_intent.terminal_state: The construction hoist is visibly at the upper work levels while the tower cranes continue operating around the unfinished building.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The building remains a recognizable, actively developing residential project throughout.

models.scene_plan: Over five seconds, begin immediately with a measured crane slew and a visible construction hoist ascending the central facade. Keep the frontal view fixed so the unfinished building stays the focal target; subtle work-site movement continues without becoming a separate event. Near the end, the hoist arrives at an upper-floor work level while both cranes remain in steady operation.
models.positive_prompt: The tower cranes slowly slew as the construction hoist rises along the unfinished residential building; small activity continues on the upper floors. Fixed frontal camera. By the final frame, the hoist has reached the upper work level and the building remains clearly an active construction site.

models.scene_plan: Use the five seconds for one continuous construction-progress action: the central hoist travels upward at an even pace while one crane pivots slowly overhead. Maintain a fixed frontal camera because the facade and vertical ascent provide the clearest evidence of progress. The movement carries through most of the shot and resolves with the hoist at the upper working floors near the end.
models.positive_prompt: A tower crane slowly turns above the unfinished apartment building while the central construction hoist climbs upward. Fixed frontal view of the building. End with the hoist at the upper floors, visibly showing steady construction progress.

models.scene_plan: For the four-second shot, make the construction hoist’s upward travel the compact primary motion, beginning at once and climbing through nearly the full duration. Pair it with one restrained overhead crane slew as visible environmental motion. Keep the camera fixed on the tower; end as the hoist nears the upper work level, preserving the clear sense of a building actively being completed.
models.positive_prompt: Fixed frontal camera on the unfinished residential tower. The central construction hoist rises steadily as a tower crane gently slews above it. In the final frame, the hoist is near the top work level and the building is still visibly under active construction.
